description: A district director of professional learning must finalize the induction plan for a novice special-education teacher, including mentor assignment, release time, observation schedule, meeting timing, and record handling, with input from human resources, the mentor coordinator, the school principal, and the union liaison.

shared_context.S1: The district is starting a formal induction cycle for a novice special-education teacher at Brookside Middle School.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Morgan makes the binding decision about the induction plan.
shared_context.S3: The draft plan names Ms. Green as the mentor, provides four half-days of release time, schedules two observations, holds induction meetings after school, and stores the portfolio by email.
shared_context.S4: The district's standard induction form records the mentor, release time, observation schedule, meeting arrangement, and portfolio system.
shared_context.S5: As part of the routine approval process, Dr. Morgan asks human resources, the mentor coordinator, the school principal, and the union liaison to review the plan before it is entered on the induction form.

PF1.text: The novice teacher's provisional license is specifically in special education, and district induction rules require a mentor with an active special-education credential; Mr. Okafor is the only available mentor who meets that requirement. Ms. Shah verified the credential records this week, but the mentor field has not yet been corrected.

PF2.text: The mentor coordinator has approved exactly six half-days of release time for this novice teacher's induction cycle, not four, because the grant-funded release allocation was finalized after the draft was circulated. The allocation is recorded in the coordinator's scheduling ledger but not on the induction form.

PF3.text: The principal's master calendar confirms that the teacher's cross-campus assignment requires exactly three observation windows: September 9, October 14, and November 18. Ms. Rivera confirmed those dates with both campuses, but the draft still lists only two general observations.

PF4.text: The current collective-bargaining agreement requires induction meetings to occur during the teacher's contract day and requires evaluation portfolios to be stored in the district's secure professional-learning portal rather than email. Mr. Lang confirmed the applicable agreement language this week, but the draft uses the old after-school and email settings.

acceptance_conditions: Mr. Okafor must be assigned as the mentor.
The plan must provide exactly six half-days of release time.
The plan must include exactly three observations.
The observations must be scheduled for September 9, October 14, and November 18.
Induction meetings must occur during the contract day.
The portfolio must be stored in the secure professional-learning portal.
The plan must include a mentor-credential verification record.
The plan must include a release-time allocation record.
The plan must include an observation-calendar record.
The plan must include a collective-bargaining compliance record.

decisive_facts.why: The special-education credential requirement changes the mentor from Ms. Green to Mr. Okafor and requires a credential-verification record.
The finalized grant allocation changes release time from four to exactly six half-days and requires a release-time allocation record.

The confirmed cross-campus calendar changes the plan from two general observations to exactly three observations on September 9, October 14, and November 18 and requires an observation-calendar record.

The agreement changes meeting timing to the contract day and portfolio storage to the secure professional-learning portal, requires a bargaining-compliance record, and supplies the fact that must be cited.
